_note: Shared fill-in lines for every 11 report (all 12 Soul Urges). Keys: EX and LP = her Expression / Life Path (1-9, 11, 22; a 33 uses 6). REASON = one-digit Life Path mod 3 (11->2, 22->4, 33->6). Every line must read right in all 12 reports, so none may name or lean on one Soul Urge's subject. Frames each field drops into are in product/0-REPORT-WORKFLOW-11.md, 'The shared list'. PY = the number of the year that starts on her next birthday (month + day + that year, to one digit; lib11_assemble.year_ahead). Its line drops into: 'Your birthday, {{NEXT_BDAY}}, starts a new year for you, and I can see what kind of year it is. {{PY.ahead}}'

1.trait: You don't wait to be asked. While everyone else is still talking it over, you've already started, and half of it's done.
1.saw: someone who went first while everyone else looked at their shoes
1.praise: Without somebody like you willing to move before it's safe, most good plans would still be sitting on a kitchen table somewhere.
1.use: the part of you that stepped up so they didn't have to
1.letter: you never waited to be told. You'd already started before anybody else had made up their mind.
1.never: Nobody since has gone first the way you did. Everybody I know stands around waiting to see who'll move, and most of the time nobody does.
1.moment: Every time a room full of people got stuck arguing over who should do something, you'd just stand up and do it, and the rest would trail after you like it had been their idea. I trailed after you too. I never said how much braver I was with you out front.
1.last: Somebody out there is going to say "we really should" one day, and you'll have the ladder out before they've finished. I hope they can keep up.

2.trait: People tell you things they've never told anybody, because you put down what you're doing and let them get all the way to the end.
2.saw: someone who'd sit still and really listen, and make room for them
2.praise: Most folks are only waiting for their turn to speak. Being really heard is something people can go a long time without, and you hand it out for free.
2.use: your ear, the one that always had time for them
2.letter: you'd stop what you were doing when I talked. You heard the whole thing, even the parts that went nowhere.
2.never: Nobody since has listened to me all the way to the end. They're always waiting for a gap so they can get their turn.
2.moment: Whenever somebody needed to talk, you'd go still and let them get it all out, however long it ran and however much it wandered. I watched people walk away from you lighter. I never admitted I was a little jealous of every one of them.
2.last: The one you let in next gets somebody who'll put the remote down and take in every bit, dull stretches and all. I hope they know their luck.

3.trait: Ten minutes after you walk into a quiet kitchen, everybody's talking, and even the shy one in the corner is telling a story.
3.saw: someone who lit up a room and made them feel like somebody
3.praise: That's worth more than people give it credit for. Somebody who'd have spent the whole night by the wall goes home feeling like they belonged, because you were there.
3.use: the part of you that made them look good
3.letter: people perked up when you were around. You asked me things like my answer mattered.
3.never: Not one person since has warmed up a room the way you did, or pulled a story out of me without even trying.
3.moment: Whenever you came along somewhere I'd sworn would be dull, inside ten minutes I'd catch people who didn't even like each other laughing with you. Afterward I'd act like it was nothing special. I was so proud of you I couldn't say it out loud.
3.last: The next person at your side will walk into a crowd of strangers with you and leave with three new friends, and they'll think they did it themselves.

4.trait: If you say you'll be there at nine, nobody bothers to call and check, because you've never once left anybody waiting.
4.saw: someone who stayed put and kept their word
4.praise: Money can't buy that. Anybody who's been let down before can finally stop bracing for the worst when you're around.
4.use: the part of you that showed up every single time
4.letter: you said you'd be there and you were. You weren't going anywhere, and I knew it.
4.never: Nobody since has been as good as their word as you were. I keep a backup plan for everybody now, and I never once needed one for you.
4.moment: Whenever I needed somebody, at any hour, I never had to think twice about who to ask. You'd say you were coming, and you'd come, no excuses and no lecture. I never once doubted you, so I never thanked you the way I should have.
4.last: Anybody who has you next gets to quit watching the clock. I hope they never take that for granted the way I did.

5.trait: Somebody suggests a last-minute trip and you've got your coat on before they finish the sentence. The best stories people tell have you in them.
5.saw: someone with some life in them, game for just about anything
5.praise: Lots of folks keep promising themselves they'll do something fun one of these weekends, and never do. Half of what they'll remember when they're old, you talked them into.
5.use: the part of you that livened things up for them
5.letter: you were up for anything. Whatever I came up with, you were in before I'd finished saying it.
5.never: Everybody since needs a week's notice and a good reason. Not one of them has ever said yes to something just to see what happens.
5.moment: You were always the one who wanted to try the place nobody'd heard of, or the thing everybody else stood back from. You'd talk me into it, and I'd complain the whole time. I never told you those were the times I laughed hardest.
5.last: Some lucky person is going to get a phone call on a dull Saturday and end up somewhere they'd never have gone alone. I hope they say yes.

6.trait: You're the one people call when something's gone wrong, and you never send a bill for it.
6.saw: someone who took care of everybody and never kept score
6.praise: And they were right. People like you hold everybody else together, and most of you go without a word of thanks for it.
6.use: all the ways you made their life easier
6.letter: you saw to everybody. Whoever needed something got it, and you never made anybody feel they owed you.
6.never: Not one person since has looked after me without keeping track of it. Everybody else's help comes with a tab, and sooner or later they hand it to me.
6.moment: Whenever somebody we knew was in trouble, you'd already be there doing something about it, and you'd never bring it up after. Half the time they didn't even know who'd helped. I knew, and I never told you how proud of you that made me.
6.last: Whoever gets you in their life next is getting somebody who'll show up with soup before they've even said they're sick. I hope they know it.

7.trait: Not much gets past you: a new haircut, a word left out of a story, a price that crept up a dollar since last week.
7.saw: someone who noticed things other people walked right past
7.praise: Everybody needs one person around with eyes like yours. Without you, the small thing nobody caught turns into the big thing everybody's stuck dealing with.
7.use: the part of you that noticed what they missed
7.letter: you caught the little things nobody else did. Not much got by you.
7.never: Nobody since notices a thing about me unless I point it out. You'd have caught it before I opened my mouth.
7.moment: Every time we were out with people, you'd pick up on what was going on underneath: what had changed, who was saying one thing and meaning another. Later you'd tell me, and you'd be right. I never said so, but it scared me a little, how much you could see.
7.last: Somebody's going to come home in a new sweater, or with a rotten afternoon behind them, and never have to point at either. You'll have seen both from the door.

8.trait: Hand you a mess and you'll have it sorted by suppertime, the bills paid, the paperwork filed, and everybody knowing what they're supposed to do.
8.saw: someone who could walk into a mess and straighten it out
8.praise: Every group of people needs one like you. Take that person away and things pile up, nobody knows who's doing what, and everybody's blaming everybody else.
8.use: the part of you that got things done
8.letter: you were the one who handled things. Something needed doing, you did it, no fuss.
8.never: Nobody since has taken a single thing off my hands. Whatever goes wrong now just sits there, waiting on me to get to it.
8.moment: Whenever something went wrong, you'd sit down with it, work out who to call and what came first, and by the end of the day it was handled and everybody knew their part. I'd have let half of it slide. I never admitted how much I leaned on that.
8.last: Lucky them, whoever's with you next. They'll get to sleep through a crisis for once and wake up to find it all in order.

9.trait: Everybody else has written somebody off, and you're still saying they've had a hard year and deserve one more chance.
9.saw: someone who'd give to anybody and look for the good in them first
9.praise: Some folks only turn things around because one person kept a door open for them. You're the one who keeps it open.
9.use: the part of you that kept on giving
9.letter: you thought the best of me. Even when I hadn't earned it, you'd find some reason to.
9.never: Nobody since has let me start over clean. Every mistake I make now gets brought up again later, usually when I least expect it.
9.moment: Whenever somebody messed up, you'd take them aside quietly instead of making a show of it, and more often than not they'd turn it around and do better by you. I watched you do it again and again. I never told you I'd have given up on most of them.
9.last: One day someone new is going to slip up in front of you and get a cup of coffee and another try instead of a lecture.

11.trait: Nobody has to explain themselves to you. You'll say out loud the thing they couldn't find words for, and they'll say that's exactly it.
11.saw: someone who knew what they needed before they'd said a word
11.praise: Being understood that fast is what most folks want their whole life and never get. Whoever had you got to stop being lonely for a while.
11.use: the part of you that kept track of their moods
11.letter: you could tell what was going on with me from my face. I never had to explain myself.
11.never: People since have cared about me, and I still have to spell out every last thing for them.
11.moment: Whenever I came to you upset, I'd talk about anything except the real thing, the weather, the traffic, whatever was handy. You'd let me go on a while, then say the one sentence I couldn't, and I'd just nod. I never told you what a relief that was, not once.
11.last: Whoever's beside you next gets to walk in the door upset and hear you say it for them. Most people never get that once.

22.trait: Starting from next to nothing has never stopped you. You'll take some odds and ends and a few borrowed hands and build something that's still standing long after.
22.saw: someone who could start with next to nothing and build something real
22.praise: Most of what's still standing anywhere got built by a handful of people with your kind of grit. Everybody else was waiting for permission.
22.use: the part of you that did the heavy lifting
22.letter: you could make something out of whatever you had. You didn't wait around for it to be handed to you.
22.never: Nobody since builds anything. They all wait for the right time and the right help and the go-ahead from somebody, and none of it ever comes.
22.moment: Every time somebody said a thing couldn't be done without more help, you'd start in with whatever was lying around and keep at it till it stood. I'd say out loud it would never work. I never once said I was wrong.
22.last: Give you a few loose boards and somebody else's bad idea, and you'll turn it into something that lasts. Whoever gets that next had better stick around.

1.trait: And when something breaks, nobody has to come rescue you. It's fixed, paid for, or worked around before most people would have finished asking for help.
1.then: When it went wrong with them, you put your head down and handled it by yourself. You didn't call anybody or let on. If something needed fixing, you fixed it, and if you couldn't, you went without. Asking would have meant explaining, and you'd had enough of being at somebody's mercy. Doing it alone got you through, and back then it made sense.
1.praise: Standing on your own two feet like that takes guts most people never find. Plenty of grown adults still freeze at a flat tire or a late bill.
1.now: you tell them you've got it before they've even offered, and soon enough they take you at your word and leave you be
1.admire: I used to brag that you never needed rescuing. Whatever broke, you'd have it fixed or figured out before anybody else knew there was a problem. I liked that about you more than I ever let on.
1.letter: When something went wrong, you dealt with it and I heard about it after, if I heard at all. You never once came to me with it. I'd made sure coming to me got you nowhere.

2.trait: And give two people who haven't spoken in weeks one evening with you in the room, and they're passing each other the salt.
2.then: When it went wrong with them, you said yes before you'd had a chance to think, and then lay awake sore about it. You kept checking where you stood, reading every look for a sign you were still liked. Keeping the peace kept things from getting worse, and when you didn't know what else to do, it was how you held on.
2.praise: That warmth of yours is a real strength. People make up and stay close because somebody like you won't let a grudge settle in.
2.now: you go along with all of it, then hold it against them on the quiet, till they feel something's off and drift away without ever knowing what
2.admire: I was proud of how you could get two people who weren't speaking to sit down and talk it out. I watched you do it with folks who swore they never would.
2.letter: You'd agree to anything I said, and a day later it'd come out sideways. You kept asking if we were okay. I never gave you a straight answer, and I knew what that did to you.

3.trait: And on the worst day of somebody's year, you can still get a real laugh out of them, and that laugh gets them through the week.
3.then: When it went wrong with them, you made a joke of it before anybody else could. You filled every day so full there wasn't a quiet minute left to think in. People asked and got the funny version, and the real thing stayed put. That got you through. If you'd stopped long enough to say it, you'd have had to feel it, and you weren't ready to.
3.praise: Not many folks can lighten a heavy room without making light of what's wrong. People breathe easier for an hour just because you're in it.
3.now: you crack a joke the minute it gets close to anything real, and after a while they quit trying
3.admire: Whenever things got tense, you'd find the one thing to say that had everybody laughing, and it never came at anybody's expense. I loved watching a room loosen up around you.
3.letter: When something bothered you, you'd get funny and find a job that needed doing. I don't think I ever heard you say what was really wrong. I never asked. It was easier on me that way.

4.trait: And anything that passes through your hands gets done properly, checked twice, and finished, so it never has to be done again.
4.then: When it went wrong with them, you got organized. You made rules for yourself and stuck to them. You worked till you dropped and went back over everything a second time, then checked it again. If every last thing was done right, nothing could catch you out. When nothing else would hold still, that was something you could hold on to, and it worked.
4.praise: That kind of care is what people trust with the important stuff, the things that can't be allowed to go wrong. Nobody hands those to someone sloppy.
4.now: you've got a way things have to be done, and you watch how they do it, till they feel checked up on and give up
4.admire: Anything you put your hands to came out right and stayed that way. I used to show your work off to people like I'd had some part in it. That was all you.
4.letter: When something got to you, you'd start making lists. You'd do things over that were fine the first time, and you wouldn't let up till it was all just so. A lot of what you were holding together was my mess. I know that.

5.trait: And change doesn't rattle you. Put you somewhere new, with faces you've never seen, and before long people are waving you over like they've known you forever.
5.then: When it went wrong with them, you changed the scenery. Different place, different people, and every time you meant it to be the clean start. Sitting still meant sitting in it, and you couldn't. Moving on gave you air when you were short of it, and it got you out from under something heavy. Back then, that was the right instinct.
5.praise: Not everybody can walk into something brand new without flinching. That kind of nerve is beyond most folks, and they stay stuck because of it.
5.now: you're itching to go the minute things start to feel ordinary, and they're left standing there wondering what they did
5.admire: I liked how easy change sat on you. Whatever got thrown at you, you'd adjust and find your feet faster than anybody I knew, and it never stopped impressing me.
5.letter: When something got to you, you were halfway out the door before anybody knew anything was wrong. A lot of the time it was me you were getting away from. I can see that now.

6.trait: And whatever's missing, you've already handled it. The extra chair's out, the coffee's on, and whoever needed a hand has had one before anybody thought to ask.
6.then: When it went wrong with them, you took care of everybody in sight. If people were busy being helped by you, nobody was close enough to see how you were doing. You ran yourself ragged, and some nights you were fed up with all of them and never said so. Being the one everybody needed gave you somewhere to stand, and it kept you going.
6.praise: Kindness like that is the reason sick folks get visited and nobody gets forgotten. Everybody around you is better off for it.
6.now: you jump in and start taking care of them, and there's never an opening for them to do a thing for you, so they go find somebody who'll let them
6.admire: You never missed a thing anybody was short of. I used to tell people you'd have what somebody needed before they'd noticed they needed it, and you never once wanted thanks.
6.letter: When something upset you, you'd go make yourself useful to somebody. Everybody got your time but you, and you'd end up worn out and mad about it. I let you carry me right along with the rest of them. That's on me.

7.trait: And it's hard to sell you a story. You'll go quiet, dig until you've got the real answer, and when you finally say what you think, it holds up.
7.then: When it went wrong with them, you clammed up, chewed on it, and wouldn't move till you were sure. You had good reason to. Late at night, on your own, you went over it and over it, hunting for the one thing that would settle it. You'd been hurt, and going quiet kept you standing while it had to.
7.praise: A careful head like yours is worth a lot. You're the one who asks the question everybody else was too polite or too rushed to ask.
7.now: you clam up and wait till you're sure of them, and before long you've found what's wrong with them
7.admire: I trusted your judgment over my own. Once you'd made up your mind about somebody, I quit arguing with you, because nine times out of ten you'd turn out right.
7.letter: When something got to you, you'd go real quiet. You'd turn it over in your head for days and you wouldn't budge, not till you knew for certain. I gave you plenty to turn over. I know that too.

8.trait: And in a crisis, people turn and look at you. You make the calls, you keep everything running, and you never once look like you're about to fold.
8.then: When it went wrong with them, you took the wheel and kept both hands on it. You made the decisions, you kept everything running, and you didn't let one person see you need a thing. If you were in charge, nobody could pull the floor out from under you again. Staying on top of it held you together when you had every reason to fold.
8.praise: Steadiness like yours is what gets everybody through a bad stretch. Plenty of people crack long before you'd even blink.
8.now: you take over everything and won't let them so much as carry a bag for you, till they feel like hired help and stop coming around
8.admire: Whenever everything went wrong at once, you'd have it in hand and everybody where they needed to be before I'd worked out what happened. I thought nothing on earth could rattle you.
8.letter: When something knocked you down, you'd grab the reins tighter. I never once saw you ask anybody for a hand. With me around, you'd have been a fool to. I'm the one who taught you that.

9.trait: And there isn't a collection jar, a fundraiser, or a stranger down on their luck that you can walk past. Whoever's struggling, near or far, gets something from you.
9.then: When it went wrong with them, you gave. You gave to good causes and to people you'd never meet, to anybody whose story got to you, and you meant every bit of it. Up close was another matter. You kept the people nearby at a little distance, even the good ones. Giving from a distance let you go on caring at all, after caring up close had cost you so much.
9.praise: A heart like yours is what keeps food banks stocked and shelters open, and the folks it helps hardly ever learn a name.
9.now: you're kind to them the way you're kind to strangers, warm but at arm's length, and the first time they let you down, you're done
9.admire: You could never walk past anybody who was struggling. I'd watch you give to people you'd never see again without even slowing down, and I bragged about it more than you know.
9.letter: When something got to you, you'd go do something good for a stranger. You never expected much from the people right in front of you. I'm a big part of the reason.

11.trait: And you read a room before you're through the door. Somebody's upset and you know it before they've said a word, and you're usually right.
11.then: When it went wrong with them, you started reading into everything. A short answer or a door shut a little too hard, and you'd be up half the night working out what it meant. Most of the time there was something there to see. Watching that close was how you saw trouble coming before it got to you, and back then you needed that.
11.praise: That's a real gift, and I don't say that lightly. Most people go their whole lives missing what you catch in a second.
11.now: you read a whole lot into one offhand thing they say, and they get tired of answering for things they never meant
11.admire: Half the fun of going anywhere with you was hearing, on the way out, everything you'd picked up that nobody had said. I'd bet against you, and I lost every time.
11.letter: Anything bothered you and you'd go hunting for what it meant. A look from me could put you off for a week, and I knew it. I gave you reasons to keep watching me. I won't pretend I didn't.

22.trait: And long before anybody else has thought about next year, you've worked out what it'll take, step by step, and which piece has to go in first.
22.then: When it went wrong with them, you worked the whole thing out in your head, a long way down the road, and wouldn't start anything till every piece was in place. Other people saw you standing still. To you it was the only way not to get caught out twice, and it made sense.
22.praise: Thinking ahead like that is what gets people through the lean stretches nobody else saw coming. Most folks can't plan past next week.
22.now: you need to know how it all ends before you'll take one step with them, and they get tired of waiting at the starting line
22.admire: It amazed me how far ahead you could see. While the rest of us took things a day at a time, you already knew what came next and how to get there.
22.letter: When something shook you, you'd sit down and think it through from start to finish before you'd so much as move. With me you never knew where anything was headed. That part's mine.

0.headline: they're too proud to be the one in the wrong
0.letter: I'm too proud. I've never once gone to anybody hat in hand, and I'm not going to start with you.

1.headline: they can't stand to be looked at by the one person who knows
1.letter: I can't face you. You know what I did, and you'd look at me like you know it.

2.headline: doing nothing doesn't cost them a thing
2.letter: Nothing happens to me if I leave it be, and I've always taken the easy way out.

1.ahead: It's a year of firsts. Something you've never done comes your way early in it, and you say yes to it. By the middle of the year you'll have a story to tell that nobody has heard from you before.

2.ahead: It's a year for people. Someone comes closer in it, slowly, the way the good ones do. It might be a friendship that deepens or someone new who's easy to be around. You won't have to chase any of it. It comes to you.

3.ahead: It's a year of good times, the kind you'd forgotten you liked. More invitations than you've had in a long while, and more laughing. Before it's half over, somebody will tell you that you look well, and they'll mean more by it than the words.

4.ahead: It's a year for setting your life up the way you want it. The room you've put off, the routine that's run too long, the thing at home that needs fixing: this is the year they get done, and they'll go easier than you expect.

5.ahead: It's a year of change, and plenty of it. A trip, a new routine, a new face, a move of some kind. Something in your life shifts in a way you didn't plan, and by the end of the year you'll be glad it did.

6.ahead: It's a year for love and home. The people close to you come closer. Somebody shows they care in a way you've waited a long time to see, and this time you let them.

7.ahead: It's a quieter year, and a good one. Things that have puzzled you for a long time come clear in it. You'll stop going over the past, because by the end of the year you'll understand it, and there'll be nothing left to go over.

8.ahead: It's a year when what you've put in starts coming back to you. A decision goes your way, or something you've worked at gets noticed. People take you more seriously in it, and you take yourself more seriously too.

9.ahead: It's a year for clearing out. Old papers, old habits, old hurts: they go. It feels like an ending at first. Then you notice how much room it's left, and what starts moving into it.
